reference_idea: Biscoff spread is so irresistible that even the devil, the most demanding taste-maker there is, gives in to it, and everybody else wants it too.

reference_decoded.stands_for: Miranda Priestly from The Devil Wears Prada: power, fashion, impossibly high standards

reference_decoded.element: The heel melting into a three-pronged devil's pitchfork
reference_decoded.stands_for: Turns 'the Devil' into a picture: the fashion icon becomes the devil herself

reference_decoded.element: The pitchfork dipping into an overflowing Biscoff jar
reference_decoded.stands_for: The devil gives in to temptation; the product is the forbidden indulgence

reference_decoded.element: Caramel spread dripping down the jar
reference_decoded.stands_for: How tempting and indulgent the product is

reference_decoded.element: 'THE DEVIL EATS BISCOFF' in a film-poster serif
reference_decoded.stands_for: A parody of the film title, with 'Wears Prada' swapped for 'Eats Biscoff' (Prada becomes Biscoff)

reference_decoded.element: Red and black type on white
reference_decoded.stands_for: Copies the film poster's look so the parody is recognised at once

reference_decoded.element: 'Don't be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.'
reference_decoded.stands_for: A twist on Miranda's line 'everybody wants to be us', meaning the product is universally wanted
Miranda's dismissive catchphrase, a final film nod

needs_to_know: The Devil Wears Prada (2006): the poster with the red stiletto and pitchfork, Miranda Priestly, assistant Andrea, and the line 'everybody wants to be us'. Without the film, it is only a shoe and a jar.

kapruka_concept.one_line: A Kapruka chocolate cake where three forks have all landed in the same last slice at once: everybody wants this, so send it to the people you love.
kapruka_concept.hook: Almost every family knows the fight over the last slice of cake. When a cake comes home, everyone goes for the same piece. It happens in Colombo and it happens in Toronto, and nobody needs a film or a phrase to get it.
kapruka_concept.visual: Flat Retail Purple (#340A5C) background with plenty of empty space. Shot from slightly above. In the lower middle: one real Kapruka chocolate cake on a plain plate, with one slice partly cut and pulled out a little. Three ordinary dessert forks are stuck into that same slice from three directions and meet in the middle. No hands, and everything stays inside the 100px margin. The cake is the thing being sent and the thing everyone wants. The single slice is the last piece everyone is after. The three forks are three different people in the house (everybody) wanting the same thing at the same moment. They also quietly echo the reference's three-pronged pitchfork. Crumbs on the plate show the cake is really being eaten, so it does not look like a catalogue shot. Nothing else in frame: no ribbons, no gold, no props.
kapruka_concept.product_role: Gifting: Kapruka cakes (a top gifting category by revenue). A real chocolate cake from the Kapruka listing, shown exactly as listed and not redesigned, is both the hero and the punchline.
kapruka_concept.why_it_makes_sense: The picture shows the forks fighting over one slice, and the headline says it straight: 'Everybody wants this.' The support line then turns that shared family moment into a gift, delivered anywhere on the island, which a sender at home or abroad understands in two seconds.

rejected: A direct film parody ('The Devil Wears…' with a red heel and a Kapruka product). Dropped because it is a third-party film trademark, it depends on knowing the film, and the red stiletto would be a borrowed prop that means nothing for Kapruka.
Showing the Biscoff jar itself as the hero. Dropped because it puts a third-party brand and logo in frame. Even if Kapruka stocks it, the standing ban on other brands' logos wins.

A chocolate box with hands from several family members reaching in from the edges of the frame. Dropped because hands cut off at the edge break the 100px margin rule, and a box of chocolates is less of a shared family moment than the last slice of cake.
warnings: I could not check the catalogue: permission for the Kapruka product-search tool was declined. So I could not confirm whether Kapruka sells Lotus Biscoff, or which exact chocolate cake listing to use. Pick a real chocolate cake listing and build the cake exactly from its photo.

Delivery scope: cakes may be delivered only to selected cities, not island-wide. Check the chosen cake with kapruka_check_delivery before using 'delivered island-wide'. If it is not island-wide, change the line to 'Kapruka cakes, delivered on the date you choose.'
The brand guidelines specify Poppins for headlines, but the standing rule says Inter, so Inter Bold 700 is used. Put 'this.' in Kapruka Yellow #FFC107 as the only highlighted word.
Three forks meeting in one slice must read in a ~250px thumbnail. Keep the forks large and clearly separated against the purple background, and drop to two forks if three looks busy.
The background is purple per the guidelines, not the reference's white. If the designer wants the reference's airy feel, Soft Cream #F5F4EB is the guideline-approved alternative.
